comment: Remote and online care is mentioned only once in the whole document, on p.133, as a reason to record whether a facility has internet. It is not listed as a component, a service, or an example under any of the seven health goals. The document treats clinical apps as sitting on top of the shared foundation (Section 5.3), which is a fair reason not to make telemedicine its own component. But the shared parts still assume the patient and the health worker are in the same building: the patient is identified at a facility, the record is tied to a facility, and the worker’s credentials are checked at a facility. Remote and store-and-forward care break these assumptions. A patient may join from home, and a specialist may read a scan or photo without ever meeting the patient. The document never checks whether the shared parts still work in these cases.

public.suggestedRevision: Add remote and online care as a named example under the health goal it fits best, and use it to test the shared components. State how the record shows who made an entry when a remote specialist reads a case without seeing the patient, how the client registry and consent service identify a patient connecting from home outside any facility, and how the workforce and facility registries confirm a provider’s identity across two facilities during an online consult.
